final_candidates.decision_summary: Conservative Leu-to-Phe substitution in the HA stem region; aromatic packing in the helical stem core is a common route to improved thermostability and environmental persistence without disrupting the fusion machinery.
Removing a surface acidic residue in the stem reduces potential electrostatic destabilization while Asn preserves polarity and can form stabilizing H-bonds; low-risk, near-isosteric change.
Small hydrophobic substitution at a stem-region Asn may improve local packing, but carries some risk of losing stabilizing H-bonds or glycosylation context, hence lower confidence.

stop_reason.detail: No external evidence available and additional self-reflection rounds are unlikely to improve the Top-3 ranking.

history.rationale: Leu-to-Phe near the end of the HA2 long helix increases hydrophobic surface area and may strengthen inter-subunit packing of the stem trimer. Conservative hydrophobic substitution with modest gain potential.
Conservative hydrophobic core/stem substitution; Leu-to-Phe often improves packing and thermostability in HA stem helices without disrupting function.
Asn-to-Ala in the HA2 helix (AELLVALENQ region) removes a polar residue from a helical segment, increasing helix propensity and removing a potential deamidation site. Low structural risk.
Lowered because removing a polar Asn in the stem region risks losing stabilizing H-bonds or glycosylation context important for HA folding.

Asp-to-Asn reduces negative charge density in the DLTDSE cluster, relieving potential electrostatic repulsion within the HA2 stem helix while preserving size and polarity. Moderate expected stability gain.
Removing a surface acidic residue can reduce electrostatic destabilization and enable H-bonding; raised above N424A which removes a potential glycosylation/H-bond donor that may aid folding.
